Similarities:
Both vegetarian and vegan diets are often driven by similar motivations, including health, ethical, and environmental concerns.

Differences:
The primary difference lies in the level of restriction regarding animal products. Vegetarians abstain from eating meat but may still consume other animal-derived products such as dairy and eggs. In contrast, vegans avoid all animal-derived products entirely, which includes items like honey and gelatin. This distinction reflects a divergence in the underlying principles concerning the use of animals and animal products.
